rows.verified: HSE Management Standards use a step-by-step risk-assessment approach for work-related stress.
The standards help organisations assess current conditions using existing data, surveys and other evidence.
The approach promotes active discussion and partnership with employees and their representatives.
The standards help identify the main work-design factors associated with work-related stress.
The framework includes identifying who may be harmed and how.
The framework requires evaluation of risks and development of practical improvements.
The process includes recording findings and agreed actions.
The framework includes monitoring and review rather than treating assessment as a one-off exercise.
Work-related stress risk depends on demands, control, support, relationships, role, change, individual factors and organisational context.
HSE stress evidence is organisation-, role-, worker-, management-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level health probability.
HSE guidance gives practical advice on controlling workplace exposure to diesel engine exhaust emissions.
Employers and self-employed people should protect employees and others who may be exposed to diesel exhaust.
Exposure to diesel engine exhaust should be prevented or controlled because the emissions contain carcinogenic substances.
Vehicle tailpipe extraction is an example of an engineering control for indoor vehicle work.
Cold or intermittently run engines can quickly create harmful exhaust concentrations indoors.
Catalytic converters should not be relied on to make indoor engine running safe.
Catalytic converters do not remove toxic oxides of nitrogen from exhaust.
Organisational controls should reduce both exposure duration and the number of people exposed.
Diesel-exhaust risk depends on engine type, fuel, load, temperature, ventilation, task duration, maintenance and worker exposure.
HSE diesel-exhaust evidence is engine-, workplace-, task-, control-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level cancer probability.
